chapters.title: Who in This World Can Escape Death?
chapters.content:
Who in this world can ever escape death?

Though you be peerless in grace and beauty, unmatched under heaven, in the end you are but rosy flesh and white bone. Though you be a favored child of heaven, ruling over ten thousand miles of rivers and mountains, in the end you will be reduced to a handful of yellow earth.

Deathless longevity—it is what all desire. But there is no ageless beauty, no immortal emperor. The fairest of maidens and the lords of a thousand years are no different from the common throng; all are trapped in the cycle of birth, age, sickness, and death. None may live forever in this world.

Yet the legend of deathless immortality has always lingered among men.

Laozi, Zhuangzi, Bodhidharma, Chen Tuan, Zhang Sanfeng—

Name after famous name echoing through the ages, like an ancient spell that forever drives later generations, making them believe that to live forever is not an absolute absurdity—that some have indeed attained that realm.

But time is the most merciless. As the years pass, even the once-undying legends are slowly ground away in the river of time.

Until, after endless silence, miracles burst forth again from the mundane.

On the night of the full moon of the fifteenth, Lan Nuo, a celestial maiden favored by heaven, would sever her mortal ties on Red Dust Peak in the Kunlun Mountains and shatter the void to ascend. Practitioners across the land were shaken to the core; the talk of longevity blazed once more into heated debate.

In recent days, over a hundred thousand people had poured into the Kunlun Mountains—from princes and nobles to peddlers and laborers, from every rank and class. They all shared the same purpose: to witness a miracle rarely seen in a thousand ages.

At last, the night of the full moon arrived. The majestic Kunlun Mountains, vast and beautiful, seemed draped in a veil of hazy moonlight, making this sacred mountain range as ethereal as a realm of immortals.

Through the moonlit night, Xiao Chen ran like the wind, his body drenched in blood, even his long black hair stained crimson. But his chiseled, handsome face held only indomitable defiance, and his eyes, bright as stars, blazed with steadfast determination.

He was fleeing for his very life!

The Royal Celestial Maiden, Zhao Lin'er, had sworn to destroy him. She led dozens of cultivators in a hunt that pressed him from all sides. Her face hidden behind a light veil, her figure willowy and graceful, her eyes like autumn waters, she moved like a startled swan—as light as a floating shadow, as ethereal as a banished immortal.

With no escape left, Xiao Chen charged toward Red Dust Peak!

Beneath the full moon, the area around Red Dust Peak was packed with people, a sea of humanity covering the hillsides. Yet a hundred thousand people gathered together were utterly silent—all of them gazing up at the white-clad woman on the summit.

On the peak, Lan Nuo stood in robes as white as snow. Bathed in the moonlight, her immortal form seemed to radiate a faint, holy light. Her white dress fluttered in the wind, and she was like the goddess of the moon, untouched by the dust of the mortal world.

Over the past half-month, she had attempted to break the void twice. Both times, at the moment of success, she had drawn back the foot she had taken.

One step away—she would live forever between heaven and earth!

But if she took that step, the endless red dust of the mortal world would forever leave her, and all earthly ties would be severed.

To draw the sword of wisdom and cut the bonds of the world—this took immense courage! For once she crossed that threshold, in the endless years of deathless longevity that awaited her, perhaps only infinite solitude would be her companion.

The heart of heaven is unfathomable; the feelings of immortals are as cold as frost.

Today, she had stood from dawn until now. Every memory of the mortal world surfaced in her heart, one after another. At last, the moment came to bid farewell to the earthly realm. A fierce radiance of sacred light suddenly erupted from the summit, covering the entire peak in a halo of supreme holiness.

Lan Nuo's skin was like ice and her bones like jade. In the sacred glow, she was so untainted, so pure. As the multitude watched in reverence, the void shattered, and she stepped forward with calm and unwavering resolve.

In that final instant, she turned her head and cast one last glance back at the mortal world. Her dreamlike, ethereal visage was forever etched into the hearts of all who saw it. A hundred thousand voices cried out Lan Nuo's name in unison.

But the orderly shouts soon broke into confusion. People saw two figures racing across the summit, hurled into the shattered void after Lan Nuo!

The chronicles of the Nine Provinces record that in the year 7316, the celestial maiden Lan Nuo broke the void through martial means and ascended to the World of Immortality. The Royal Celestial Maiden Zhao Lin'er was fortunate enough to share in this immortal fate and followed her into that realm.

As for Xiao Chen, he was not fated to be recorded in those pages.

In the instant the void shattered, Xiao Chen was shocked beyond words!

He had never imagined that such a day would come, that he would enter the World of Immortality in this manner. In that moment, his thoughts raced to many things—his family, his friends... he would never see them again. He would leave this mortal world forever.

A life-or-death escape had ended in such a result. To many, shattering the void to enter the World of Immortality was a glory that would echo through the ages. But Xiao Chen would have gladly given up this chance. He was so reluctant to leave this world—his parents, his loved ones... Farewell forever! He bid the red dust of the mortal world a silent goodbye.

Xiao Chen did not know that the Royal Celestial Maiden, Zhao Lin'er, had also shattered the void and followed into that realm.

chapters.title: The Death Castle and the Sea of Bones
chapters.content:
Rolling black clouds blotted out the light of heaven and earth, plunging everything into endless darkness. Like the curtain of death falling, a ghastly,森然 terror spread through the air. In that surging death-cloud, a towering ancient castle loomed fitfully at the edge of the sky. Crimson waves of blood rushed up from within the old fortress, casting a凄艳 red glare through the black clouds. The silence was dreadful, utterly without sound, dead quiet.

The castle bore the marks of age and沧桑, as if it had torn through time from the primordial age. It was a vortex of death, pulling the boundless death-aura of the ten directions toward itself. The churning black clouds were slowly devoured.

As the black mist faded, the high heavens grew even more陰森 and terrifying. Around the castle floated endless bones—a vast sea of white skeletons spread like a field. The森然 castle stood above that snowy sea of bone, beyond words恐怖 and死寂.

Several gray-winged humanoid skeletons flew out from the castle, their death-aura rolling down in waves as they gazed at a lonely island deep in the ocean below.

It was a solitary island in the vast sea.

On the island, forests stretched wild, with apes howling and tigers roaring. Ninety percent of the land was covered by primeval forest—ancient trees blotting out the sun, fierce beasts and birds crying and soaring—a scene of pure savagery.

But then, a wave of chilling,森然 death-aura swept in from the distant sky, and the island, which had been filled with the roars of savage beasts, gradually fell silent.

Deep within the island, it seemed some ancient beast of the洪荒 growled in anger a few times, but beyond that, there was only dead stillness.

Xiao Chen, lying unconscious on the beach, seemed to feel that piercing cold, his body trembling unconsciously.

After a long time, the陰森 death-aura slowly receded. In the far distance, the white sea of bones bearing that ancient, timeworn castle gradually disappeared over the endless ocean.

Only then did heaven and earth begin to revive. Several dozen dragon-like roars sounded from deep in the island, and the island slowly returned to its normal vitality.

The sun blazed overhead. How long had passed? Xiao Chen woke from unconsciousness. The sound of waves reached his ears. He slowly opened his eyes to see the blue-green sea rolling before him. He was lying on the hot golden sand.

The scorching sun made him dizzy and feverish, his whole body burning with pain. His mouth was dry, his lips cracked. He struggled to sit up and surveyed this unfamiliar place.

The hot wind brought the salty smell of the sea. Flocks of seabirds soared over the blue water, and huge fish occasionally leaped up, stirring great waves.

From deep in the island came the roars of various savage beasts, thundering like heaven's drums. Xiao Chen felt as if he had returned to the age of myth!

By the shore, a grove of lush coconut trees cast patches of shade. Clusters of ripe brownish-yellow coconuts hung together, enticing against the green leaves.

His dry mouth seemed to produce some saliva. He forced himself to stand and staggered forward.

The sun was blocked, and the burning pain faded.

A little sea breeze blew, rustling the green coconut fronds. Xiao Chen finally felt a trace of coolness.

Ripe coconuts occasionally fell to the ground with a thud.

His throat felt like flames were flickering inside; smoke seemed to come from his mouth. Xiao Chen was parched beyond measure, his whole body aching. He stumbled, gathered a pile of coconuts, and then plopped down to sit on the sand.

He used his energy to crack open a coconut and drank the sweet, refreshing juice in big gulps. It was wonderful. To someone as dry as he was, it felt like the finest nectar.

So he had come to the World of Immortality!

Xiao Chen's thoughts were tangled. Where had Lan Nuo gone? And those legendary figures from the ages—did they truly live in this world? He was full of questions. Of course, he did not know that the Royal Celestial Maiden Zhao Lin'er had also entered this realm.

Finally, he knelt silently on the ground, bowing across time and space to his parents. From now on, immortal and mortal would be forever separated!

He was a decisive person. He forced himself to set aside his失落 feelings and began to consider how to survive in this strange world.

Sitting quietly on the sand, leaning against a thick coconut tree, a faint luster shimmered on Xiao Chen's skin, as if a hazy glow enveloped his body. The essence of heaven and earth gathered continuously, and within the coconut grove, spiritual energy swirled, with faint rose-colored light drifting.

Roars of beasts came incessantly. This was no peaceful land. His first task was to recover his body as soon as possible. Xiao Chen circulated his cultivation technique, guiding the vegetative essence, and began to heal his injuries.

His method of cultivation came from a mysterious stone carving.

He had grown up by the Yellow River. When he was seven years old, a rare drought struck, and the Yellow River near his village nearly dried up. A huge stone stele emerged from the riverbed. Once the mud was cleared away, four ancient characters were carved on the front: Ever-Pacify the Yellow River!

An ancient legend had long been passed down along the Yellow River—that when Yu the Great controlled the floods, a divine stele had descended from the Nine Heavens to settle forever in the river, ensuring no more floods.

Thus, when the stele emerged from the Yellow River, the villagers immediately thought of the old legend. They cleaned the mud from the stele and burned incense and worshipped it day and night.

Once it was thoroughly cleaned, the back of the stele also revealed carvings—a mysterious and complex diagram. The villagers could not understand it and took it for a heavenly script.

That "heavenly script" filled the young Xiao Chen with endless wonder. Every day he would go and stare at the stele, until two months later when heavy rains fell continuously, the river rose, and the stele sank forever to the bottom.

But by then, that mysterious and complex diagram was already deeply etched into young Xiao Chen's mind. Later, when he began to learn martial arts and walk the path of cultivation, he finally understood what that complex stone carving was!

It was an ancient and mysterious Heaven-Bestowed Qi-Refining Diagram!

Xiao Chen did not know if that mysterious stone carving could compare to the legendary celestial scriptures and precious tomes. From the age of ten, he had begun to cultivate it unceasingly. For the next ten years, he constantly learned combat techniques from others, but he never changed his core method.

chapters.title: The Eight-Armed Malignant Dragon
chapters.content:
Ten years of bitter cultivation of the mysterious stone carving had deeply benefited Xiao Chen. His physique was constantly changing, and he vaguely felt as if he had been reborn, his bones and flesh remade. Yet what ultimately gave him faith in this Qi-Refining Diagram was a fierce battle deep in the Kunlun Mountains.

He had gone to witness Lan Nuo's divine act of breaking the void, but on the way, he was insulted by the guards of the Royal Celestial Maiden. That was the most desperate fight of his life. He cut down thirteen royal iron guards to break free, and in the chaos, he slew Zhao Lin'er's personal maidservant.

This proved that the mysterious stone carving was no ordinary scripture. Ten years of bitter cultivation had allowed his skills to reach a respectable level.

Day after day of practice deepened Xiao Chen's understanding of the Heaven-Bestowed Qi-Refining Diagram, and the more he understood, the more he felt it must have a continuation. He sensed that this was not a complete cultivation method!

Legend said that the stele bearing the inscription 'Ever-Pacify the Yellow River' had fallen from the Nine Heavens. Perhaps there were other divine steles like it, but the chance of obtaining the subsequent inscriptions was slim indeed!

Sunlight, moonlight, the essence of plants and trees... The natural world held endless primordial energy, countless forms of power. In the coconut grove, Xiao Chen circulated his refinement technique, drawing in the essence of heaven and earth to nourish his wounded body. A faint, misty glow surrounded him.

Two hours later, he emerged from his meditative stillness. His injuries were less severe than he had imagined. He estimated he could fully recover within ten days.

The red sun was setting in the west, its dying rays spilling across the sea, painting it a vivid crimson. The ocean met the sky; seawater, misty clouds, a stretch of fading red.

Then—"Boom!" "Boom!" "Boom!"—the beach began to tremble. Heavy, dull sounds reached Xiao Chen's ears. He turned to look, and his face instantly changed.

A silver behemoth crawled up from the sea onto the shore. Its body was a full fifty meters long. At first glance, it looked like a silver crocodile the size of a mountain, but upon closer inspection, the differences were clear.

Along its spine, like a silver mountain range, stood over a hundred enormous bone spikes, each two meters long, gleaming coldly. They rose like a forest of sharp spears, guarding its rear.

It was simply colossal. Its entire body was covered in gleaming silver scales, each over a meter long and half a meter wide. From afar, this silver giant, shimmering with cold light, looked utterly ferocious.

The silver beast had eight thick, powerful clawed arms. At the ends of those arms, sharp giant claws glinted with a somber light, chilling to behold. Moreover, it bore on its head a single, sharp horn seven or eight meters long, flickering with cold silver radiance. This was truly a terrifying giant monster.

Its jade-green eyes, huge as millstones, gave off torch-like ghostly light. It swept its gaze across the shoreline, then lumbered onto the sand.

Facing the setting sun, it opened its bloody maw, revealing a row of meter-long fangs like broadswords. It let out a terrifying roar that shook the nearby sea. The waves churned violently. Seabirds in the sky fled in terror, and some closer ones plunged straight into the ocean.

Such power! It truly shook heaven and earth!

Though Xiao Chen had covered his ears at once, they still rang with a deafening buzz. The colossal roar was like thunder exploding right beside him.

After roaring at the setting sun, the fifty-meter-long giant beast crouched on the sand, closed its huge eyes, and seemed to intend to rest here.

Xiao Chen was deeply shaken. The World of Immortality was indeed extraordinary!

Gazing at the silver behemoth like a mountain ridge, he remembered the ancient ferocious beast of seafaring legend—the Eight-Armed Malignant Dragon!

This hideous, terrifying giant was exactly the same as the Eight-Armed Malignant Dragon of legend!

Legend said that the ancient beast could overturn rivers and seas, summon wind and rain. Any ship that encountered it was doomed to destruction. It was the most savage monster in the ocean; even the Sea God would flee at the sight of it!

"A primordial savage beast that can rival gods... actually exists in this world!" Remembering those ancient tales, Xiao Chen's face was filled with shock. He had never thought that in the World of Immortality, he would witness such a legendary monster with his own eyes.

Though he was far away, Xiao Chen could already feel the fierce, baleful aura. This colossal ancient beast had torn apart countless sea creatures in its time!

Xiao Chen was very rational. He stood up, moved lightly, and slowly walked deeper into the coconut grove. Only when he was certain the ancient beast could not detect him did he stop and watch from a distance.

The Eight-Armed Malignant Dragon was like a silver mountain range, lying still and silent, as if turned to stone. Xiao Chen guessed that this beach might be its resting place, and it would probably sleep here through the night.

Ever since the ancient beast climbed onto the shore and roared at the setting sun, the nearby primeval forest had fallen silent. Only deep within the island came the howls of savage beasts.

A gentle sea breeze blew, and the evening glow was fading. In the dense forest by the sea, Xiao Chen startled countless birds into flight. The ground was covered with bird eggs—dinner was settled.

Moonlight flowed like water under a canopy of stars. Waves lapped gently against the sand. A faintly salty sea breeze stirred softly in the night. Xiao Chen slowly drifted into sleep in the coconut grove.

At dawn, a red sun rose. Golden light spread across the sea's horizon.

A soul-shaking, ear-splitting roar pierced the clouds!

The legendary ancient beast, the Eight-Armed Malignant Dragon, was opening its bloody maw at the sun just rising above the ocean, bellowing a sky-shaking roar. The calm blue morning sea surged up from the sheer force of the sound waves. The seabirds that had been flying across the sky vanished in terror.

The massive silver dragon moved all eight arms and claws. The beach rumbled as it slowly stepped into the sea. The calm ocean instantly boiled like a tsunami, sending up towering waves as the silver form thrashed in the water.

Only when it gradually faded into the distance did the sea slowly calm down.

The tide rose and fell. The seawater washed away all traces of the dragon from the shore.

0001.title: Chapter 1: The Ascent of Lan Nuo
0001.content:
The novel opens with a philosophical hammer blow: ‘Who in this world can ever escape death?’ It’s a direct, solemn question that sets the tragic, desolate tone for everything to follow. Chen Dong isn’t asking for show—this is the central wound of the story. Immortality is the dream, but the cost is absolute: separation from family, from the mortal world, from everything that makes life worth living.

We’re then thrown into the moonlit ascension of Lan Nuo on Red Dust Peak. The crowd of a hundred thousand is silent. She’s described as a celestial maiden, white garments like snow, surrounded by sacred radiance. It’s a ritualistic, breathtaking scene—but the real action is at the base of the peak, where Xiao Chen is running for his life, drenched in blood, pursued by the Royal Celestial Maiden Zhao Lin’er.

This contrast is the heart of the chapter: pure, divine grace on the peak versus desperate, bloody survival at its foot. Xiao Chen is not a willing pilgrim to the World of Immortality. He’s a fugitive forced through the void by accident, and his internal monologue is not triumphant but grieving. He thinks of his parents, his home, his reluctance to leave. This is a protagonist who carries his tragedy from page one.

Lan Nuo herself is not a cold goddess. She hesitated—twice—before stepping through the void. Her final glance back at the mortal world is poignant. And in that moment, Xiao Chen and Zhao Lin’er are pulled along with her. The chapter ends with a historical chronicle entry: ‘In 7316, the divine maiden Lan Nuo broke the void; Princess Zhao Lin’er was fortunate to accompany her into the World of Immortality. As for Xiao Chen, he was not recorded in history.’ A perfect, cold epitaph that underscores his anonymity—and sets up a protagonist who will have to earn his place.

This chapter is a masterclass in establishing tone: tragic, mythic, and deeply human. It hooks you with the question of mortality and leaves you with a protagonist who has lost everything except his will to survive.

0002.title: Chapter 2 Guide: The Death Castle and the Divine Stele
0002.content:
Chapter 2 opens with one of the most iconic images in the entire novel: the Death Castle, an ancient, eerie fortress floating over a vast sea of bones, surrounded by gray-winged humanoid skeletons. This is a direct contrast to the tranquil tropical island where Xiao Chen wakes shortly after. The shift from deathly dread to vibrant, sun-drenched jungle sets up a core theme of the novel: the constant juxtaposition of sacred and savage, life and death.

Xiao Chen’s first actions—drinking coconut water, kneeling to bid farewell to his parents—ground him as a reluctant exile, not a triumphant hero. His grief is palpable but controlled, and he quickly turns to survival. The chapter then reveals the origin of his cultivation: a childhood encounter with the Yellow River Divine Stele during a drought. The stele bears the ancient inscription 'Ever-Pacify the Yellow River' and a mysterious diagram on its reverse—the Heaven-Bestowed Qi-Refining Diagram, which Xiao Chen has practiced for ten years.

This backstory is crucial. It ties Xiao Chen to a legendary artifact and a unique cultivation path that sets him apart from ordinary practitioners. The stele’s connection to Yu the Great and the Nine Heavens hints at a grand cosmic destiny. Xiao Chen is not just a random survivor; he carries the seed of a forgotten myth.

The chapter also mentions Lan Nuo and the legendary void-breakers, establishing the larger world of immortals and the questions that will drive Xiao Chen: Where is Lan Nuo? Do those legends truly walk this world? And most importantly, how will he survive and grow in this brutal, beautiful realm?

0003.title: World of Immortality Chapter 3: The Eight-Armed Malignant Dragon
0003.content: This chapter delivers one of the novel's first truly mythic set-pieces: the emergence of a legendary sea monster, the Eight-Armed Malignant Dragon. The beast is described in staggering physical detail—fifty meters long, armored in silver scales, eight clawed arms, bone spikes like lances—and its roar alone swells the sea and drops birds from the sky. It’s a primeval creature straight out of folklore, a force of nature that even gods would flee. And Xiao Chen? He doesn’t charge in with sword drawn. He watches, retreats, and survives. That’s the core of his character here: pragmatic caution over reckless pride. He’s been cultivating for ten years from the mysterious stone carving, but he already senses his technique is incomplete. That subtle thread—the incomplete stele, the lost divine scriptures—becomes a long-term driver. But the real star is the dragon. Chen Dong’s prose turns the beach into a stage for sublime horror, contrasting peaceful sunset and coconut groves with a monster that could flatten a warship. It’s a perfect tone-setter: the World of Immortality is beautiful, vast, and utterly lethal.

0002.chapter_meta_description: In Chapter 2 of World of Immortality, Xiao Chen awakens on a tropical island after surviving the Death Castle. The chapter reveals the origin of his unique cultivation method—the Heaven-Bestowed Qi-Refining Diagram from the Yellow River Divine Stele—and sets up his reluctant journey in the World of Immortality. A tale of tragedy, myth, and survival begins.

0003.chapter_meta_description: Xiao Chen encounters the legendary Eight-Armed Malignant Dragon on the shores of Dragon Island—a fifty-meter primordial beast that rivals gods. Witness his pragmatic survival instincts and the first hint of his incomplete cultivation technique.
